meta.title: Peppobot
meta.description: Peppobot's video game log: reviews of every game played, scored on six axes, with hours tracked. Now playing, top rated and what's next.
meta.libraryDescription: Every game Peppobot has played, is playing or will play: search by title, developer, genre or platform and read the reviews.
meta.telemetryDescription: Peppobot's gaming stats: games logged, hours played, average scores, tier distribution, hours by platform and scores by genre.
meta.protocolDescription: How Peppobot reviews video games: six scoring axes from 0 to 10, criteria for each genre, score tiers and the hardware used.

hero.intro: A fake robot with REAL gaming opinions. Six-axis diagnostics, countless hours logged, questionable human judgment.

axes.name: Gameplay
axes.note: Moment-to-moment feel: controls, systems, combat, puzzles. Does it play well?

axes.name: Visuals
axes.note: Art direction first, raw tech second. Does it look like nothing else?

axes.name: Audio
axes.note: Soundtrack, sound design and voice work. Does it stay in my head?

axes.name: Genre · I
axes.note: The first criterion of the game's genre: what its kind lives or dies on.

axes.name: Genre · II
axes.note: The second criterion of the game's genre.

axes.name: Signature
axes.note: What only this game does. The thing it will be remembered for.

title: OPERATOR
telemetry.
telemetry.profileIntro: Every completed run leaves a trace. Six-axis averages reveal the operator's scoring habits. The math is mechanical. The taste is unmistakably human.

title: Scoring
protocol.
protocol.intro: Six diagnostic axes. Scores from 0 to 10. One simple average. The robot handles the math. The human is responsible for the questionable opinions. Final scores are issued only after a completed run or a meaningful review milestone.

axisCards.name: Gameplay
axisCards.note: Controls, mechanics, combat, puzzles, and moment-to-moment feel. Is the game actually fun to operate?

axisCards.name: Visuals
axisCards.note: Art direction, animation, readability, and technical execution. More polygons do not automatically mean more personality.

axisCards.name: Audio
axisCards.note: Music, sound design, and voice performances. Does it enhance the experience or just occupy bandwidth?

axisCards.name: Genre · I
axisCards.note: The primary genre-specific test. Different kinds of games require different diagnostics.

axisCards.name: Genre · II
axisCards.note: The secondary genre-specific test. Because a single genre-specific obsession was apparently insufficient.

axisCards.name: Signature
axisCards.note: The defining quality of this particular game, evaluated on its own terms. Every title gets a custom diagnostic.

title: Genre
calibration
calibration.text: Not every game runs on the same hardware. Or the same expectations. Axes 04 and 05 adapt to the genre. The other four stay consistent.

1.name: Narrative
1.note: Story, writing and choices. Does the world have something to say, and do my decisions actually change it?

1.name: Progression
1.note: Levels, skills and gear over the long run. Does getting stronger feel earned, and does it change how I play?

2.name: Story & characters
2.note: Evaluates plot, narrative pacing, dialogue quality, characterization, character relationships, and worldbuilding.

2.name: Progression
2.note: Progression depth, build variety, and customization freedom. Is developing your party rewarding?

3.name: Build & loot
3.note: Build variety, synergies, and progression. Is experimenting rewarding?

3.name: Endgame
3.note: Challenges and replayability. Is the grind fun, or is it all about the rewards?

4.name: Endgame
4.note: Content variety, rewards and replayability. Is the endgame worth coming back to?

4.name: Balance
4.note: Class, progression and competitive balance. Is the playing field fair?

5.name: Creativity
5.note: The tools to build and express. How far can I go beyond what the developers imagined?

5.name: Freedom
5.note: Open goals and systemic play. Does the world let me set my own objectives and reach them my way?

6.name: Level design
6.note: Layout, pacing and secrets. Does every stage teach something new and then put it to the test?

6.name: Controls
6.note: Jumps, momentum and precision. When I fall, is it always my fault and never the controller's?

7.name: Exploration
7.note: World design, discovery and puzzles. Does exploring reward curiosity and make every new path worth following?

7.name: Story & pacing
7.note: Story, characters and the balance between action and adventure. Does the journey stay engaging from start to finish?

8.name: Gunplay
8.note: Weapon feel, recoil, feedback and variety. Does every shot land with weight, and does each gun earn its place?

8.name: Cover & movement
8.note: Cover, mobility and positioning. Does the camera and the way I move turn every firefight into a tactical choice?

9.name: Depth
9.note: Systems, detail and fidelity. Does the simulation hold up when I look closer, and do its parts interact in believable ways?

9.name: Immersion
9.note: Routine, flow and the feeling of the role. Does doing the job become absorbing rather than a chore?

10.name: Combat system
10.note: Moveset depth, combos and the neutral game. Does mastering a character keep opening new options?

10.name: Roster & balance
10.note: Character variety and fairness. Is every pick viable, and does each one play differently?

11.name: Community
11.note: Neighbours, relationships and shared moments. Do the characters around me feel alive and worth coming back to?

11.name: Daily rhythm
11.note: Routines, seasons and small goals. Does every day give me a reason to log in without turning into a chore?

12.name: Run variety
12.note: Procedural layouts, builds and surprises. Does every run feel different from the last?

12.name: Meta progression
12.note: Unlocks and knowledge carried between runs. Does each death leave me stronger or wiser for the next one?

13.name: Discovery
13.note: Places, secrets and the pull of the unknown. Does the world keep rewarding the urge to see what's next?

13.name: Atmosphere
13.note: Mood, setting and sense of place. Does the journey leave an impression that stays after the credits?

14.name: Combat flow
14.note: Combos, crowd control and impact. Does cutting through hordes feel powerful and stay fun for hours?

14.name: Variety
14.note: Characters, weapons, enemies and missions. Does the game find new ways to keep the action fresh?

15.name: Tension
15.note: Dread, scares and pacing. Does the fear build up, or does it fade into routine?

15.name: Resource management
15.note: Ammo, healing and saves. Is scarcity a meaningful pressure that shapes every choice?

16.name: Map design
16.note: Interconnection, shortcuts and backtracking. Does the world fold back on itself in satisfying ways?

16.name: Ability gating
16.note: New powers and the paths they open. Does every upgrade change how I see the map?

17.name: Group fun
17.note: Laughs, chaos and shared moments. Does it get better the more people join in?

17.name: Accessibility
17.note: Rules, controls and onboarding. Can anyone pick it up and have fun within minutes?

18.name: Moment-to-moment
18.note: Responsiveness, rhythm and impact. Does every second of play feel sharp and satisfying?

18.name: Challenge
18.note: Difficulty curve, enemies and mastery. Does the game push me to get better and reward me when I do?

19.name: Feel of the sport
19.note: Physics, animations and controls. Does it capture what makes the sport fun to play?

19.name: Modes & longevity
19.note: Career, online and side modes. Is there enough to keep coming back season after season?

20.name: Gunplay
20.note: Weapon feel, recoil, feedback and variety. Does every shot land with weight, and does each gun earn its place?

20.name: Encounter design
20.note: Arenas, enemies and pacing. Do fights ask me to think and move, not just aim?

21.name: Tactics
21.note: Planning, information and teamwork. Do smart decisions beat fast reflexes?

21.name: Map design
21.note: Angles, routes and destructibility. Does every map open new ways to attack and defend?

22.name: Economy
22.note: Prices, demand and growth. Do my decisions move the numbers in ways I can read and learn from?

22.name: Management depth
22.note: Staff, logistics and expansion. Does running the business keep posing new problems as it grows?

23.name: Combat flow
23.note: Combos, juggles and crowd control. Does clearing a screen of enemies feel punchy and stylish?

23.name: Co-op & replay
23.note: Characters, multiplayer and unlocks. Is it worth running through again with friends?

24.name: Handling
24.note: Physics, speed and feedback. Does every car feel distinct, and does driving it well feel earned?

24.name: Tracks & modes
24.note: Circuits, events and progression. Is there enough variety to keep me racing?

25.name: Tactics
25.note: Positioning, terrain and turn economy. Does every battle reward planning over brute force?

25.name: Party building
25.note: Classes, skills and unit growth. Does shaping my squad open new ways to win?

26.name: Hero design
26.note: Abilities, roles and identity. Does every hero bring a distinct playstyle that's fun to master?

26.name: Team play
26.note: Synergies, counters and objectives. Do matches reward coordination over solo heroics?

27.name: Strategic depth
27.note: Units, resources and long-term plans. Does every turn offer meaningful choices with consequences?

27.name: Opponent & balance
27.note: AI, factions and fairness. Is the challenge smart and are the sides balanced?

28.name: Survival loop
28.note: Hunger, threats and crafting. Does staying alive keep me on edge without becoming a chore?

28.name: Building & progression
28.note: Bases, tools and technology. Does each step forward change how I face the world?

29.name: Adaptation
29.note: Rules, components and table feel. Does the digital version keep what makes the board game fun?

29.name: Play options
29.note: Online, local and AI opponents. Is it easy to find a good game at any time?

30.name: Planning
30.note: Layout, zoning and logistics. Does a well-planned city feel different from a messy one, and do I learn to build better?

30.name: Growth & challenge
30.note: Needs, crises and expansion. Does the city keep posing new problems as it grows?

31.name: Shooting & patterns
31.note: Weapons, enemy waves and bullet patterns. Is every stage a readable, thrilling dance?

31.name: Score & replay
31.note: Scoring systems, routes and difficulty. Does it pull me back to beat my best run?

32.name: Music & timing
32.note: Tracklist, charts and input feel. Does hitting the beat feel tight, and do the songs stick in my head?

32.name: Challenge & variety
32.note: Difficulty curve, modes and charts. Does it keep teaching new patterns and pushing me to improve?

33.name: Writing
33.note: Plot, prose and characters. Does the story grip me and make me care about the people in it?

33.name: Choices & structure
33.note: Branches, routes and pacing. Do my decisions matter, and is every route worth reading?

34.name: Daily life
34.note: Routines, chores and small rewards. Does living this life become cozy and absorbing rather than repetitive?

34.name: Growth & freedom
34.note: Upgrades, relationships and goals. Does my place in the world change in ways I chose?

title: Gacha
meter
gachaMeter.text: A virus scan for monetization, shown on the cover art of finished runs. Despite the name, it doesn't only look at paid pulls: premium currencies, loot boxes, battle passes, paywalls and pay-to-skip all count. It measures how hard the game pushes you to pay. It sits outside the six axes and never changes the average. Live games get scanned again when an update changes their economy.
levelNotes: Everything that matters can be earned by playing. Spending is optional and never needed to keep up.
Not pay to win, but the shop pushes hard: steep prices, artificial grind, timers or FOMO nudging you toward the wallet.
Money buys power or progress that playing can't reasonably match. Not paying means falling behind.

title: Test
bench
rig.text: Every report is filed from one of these machines. Visuals and audio are judged on what they actually show and play, so the same game may run differently on your hardware.

tierNotes.OVERCLOCKED: Exceeds all expectations. Permanently stored in core memory.
tierNotes.GLITCHED: Inconsistent output. Proceed at your own risk.

aboutText: Peppobot is a fictional robot operated by a very real human with a weakness for RPGs, roguelikes, and perfectly timed parries.
Its mission: play games, collect data, overanalyze everything, and occasionally remember that gaming is supposed to be fun.
The calculations are accurate. The opinions are entirely human.

bottomBar.credits: FAKE ROBOT. REAL OPINIONS. QUESTIONABLE TASTE.
